chunks: And Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār, and from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, both from ‘Alī ibn Ismā‘īl, from Muḥammad ibn ‘Amr al-Zayyāt, from Hārūn ibn Khārijah, who said:
I heard Abā ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) say: Whoever visits the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him), knowing his right, Allāh will register him among those in A‘lā ‘Illīyyīn.

key_terms.عَارِفاً بِحَقِّهِ: knowing his right (recognizing the spiritual status and rights of the Imam)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting the grave of Imam al-Husayn with knowledge of his rights?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this hadith from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat* elevates the visitation of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) to a cosmic act of worship, linking the physical grave to the Divine Throne. The condition of being 'knowing his right' (‘ārifan bi-ḥaqḥi) emphasizes that spiritual recognition of the Imam’s authority is prerequisite for the reward of being inscribed among the 'A‘lā ‘Illīyyīn', reflecting the Shia belief in the inseparable link between gnosis of the Imam and salvation.
